entry.title: Modern Run Dialog UI For Windows 10 & 11 6.0.2.0
entry.content:
• Fixed dialog position drift when typing (#7877): Fixed an issue where the Run dialog would jump or shift away from fixed positions (such as Bottom Left) as suggestions expanded or shrank, especially in Compact Mini-Pill Mode. Resizing now atomically preserves the configured anchor.
  • Fixed Background Opacity on Windows 11 Blur & other themes (#7902): Wired the Background Opacity (30–255) setting so it visibly adjusts the translucency/tint of Windows 11 Blur, Liquid Glass, and solid themes even when no custom background image or GIF is set.

entry.title: Windows Vista/7 Blocked Shutdown UX & Logoff Sequence 1.4
entry.content: • Fix the issue where enabling the logoff sequence makes the system automatically log on again after logging off if a user account has no password set (by @repensky)

entry.title: Independent taskbar per monitor 1.7.2
entry.content:
1.7.2

  • Pins made from a window button no longer break after the app restarts. With Disable grouping on the taskbar, the mod pins the app's Start menu shortcut instead. This is a temporary workaround for #7900, existing pins are not changed.
  • The jump list of a window button shows Pin to taskbar again if the app is only pinned on another taskbar.
  • Pinning from a window button puts the pin on that taskbar (before, it could end up on the main taskbar).
  • Fixed a rare case where pinning an app on another taskbar too moved it to the end of the pin list.
  • Code cleanup: shared helpers and automatic cleanup of system objects.

1.7.1 (not released on its own, included here)

  • Works together with mods that change taskbar grouping (e.g. Disable grouping on the taskbar, including Pinned items remain in place): pinning and unpinning from a window button now apply to the clicked taskbar. Before, Unpin could remove the pin from another taskbar.
  • Readme in English, German, Russian, French and Spanish, with animated before/after pictures and a link for reporting bugs.
  • The note about other mods is now a general hint instead of "not compatible".

entry.title: MultiWM Companion 0.3.2
entry.content:
MultiWM Companion

An optional add-on for MultiWM. Without it, a new window first appears where the app puts it, then jumps into its tile. With it, the window opens in its tile directly.

What it does

  • New windows open in the tile MultiWM will give them, with your gap, insets and window rules applied.
  • Windows restored from the taskbar or the tray reappear in their own tile.
  • Windows that will float (by a rule, in the Floating layout, or because they don't fit) open where they'll float.
  • If a guess turns out wrong (say the app resizes itself right after opening), MultiWM moves the window as usual.

Dialogs, tool windows, excluded windows, and windows that open maximized or fullscreen are left alone.

Requirements

  • MultiWM installed and running, in Automatic mode. In Manual mode this mod does nothing.
  • A matching MultiWM release (see the version chart below). Try to update MultiWM and the companion together: mismatched versions may give no hints.

Compatibility

Don't combine with other mods that move windows before they appear, such as Window Centralizer or Center New Windows: both would move the same window.

Troubleshooting

Enable logging for this mod in Windhawk to see each placement decision.

Version chart

Companion MultiWM
0.3.2 1.16.1+

entry.title: MultiWM 1.16.1
entry.content:
Functionality note

  • The bsp layout setting now means the new BSP layout. Configurations saved before 1.13.29 used bsp for Dwindle; those now open in BSP. Choose Dwindle again in the layout settings to keep the old behaviour.

New

  • BSP layout. New windows split the focused or biggest tile. Drag a window near a tile's edge to split it there, or drop it in the center to swap.
  • Resize hotkeys. Alt+= grows the focused window, Alt+- shrinks it and Alt+0 resets it. You can hold a key to repeat, and set the step size.
  • Drag preview. While you drag a tiled window, MultiWM shows where it will land. You can change the opacity, outline, corner radius, app icon size and fade time.
  • Clearer hotkey feedback. If another program already uses one of MultiWM's shortcuts, a toast names that program. A hotkey that can't do anything now tells you why.
  • Support for the MultiWM Companion mod.

Changes

  • "Set Master Window" (Alt+M) is now Layout Action. It rotates the focused split in BSP and still promotes the focused window in other layouts.
  • "Adaptive Dwindle" settings are now Adaptive Split settings and apply to BSP as well. Splits go back to normal when the extra space is no longer needed, unless you've resized a window.
  • If you change the management mode with the hotkey or tray menu, it stays that way until MultiWM restarts or you change the setting.
  • The Floating default size now applies whenever a window floats for the first time, not only in Automatic mode.

Fixes and improvements

  • Windows of apps that stop responding are handled better.
  • Minor bug fixes and improvements.

entry.title: Yandex Music Transparency 1.2.8
entry.content:
• Added configurable opacity for active and inactive windows (Alpha / InactiveAlpha).
  • Added "fully opaque on hover" option (OpaqueOnHover).
  • Added "fully opaque when maximized/fullscreen" option (OpaqueWhenMaximized), applied immediately to avoid clashing with the system resize animation.
  • Added smooth animated transitions between opacity levels (SmoothTransitions).
  • Defaults: active opacity 220, inactive opacity 170 (inactive windows are now more transparent than the active value), smooth transitions on, fully opaque on hover off.
  • Fixed restoring the original alpha on unload (the window's true original opacity is now captured once).

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 3.4.0
entry.content:
New

  • Power menu: "Update and restart" and "Update and shut down" while Windows has updates waiting, like the Start menu's. UpdatesWaiting() reads whether either of Windows' own pending-reboot keys exists (WindowsUpdate\Auto Update\RebootRequired or Component Based Servicing\RebootPending, KEY_WOW64_64KEY since the island is 32-bit), once each time the menu opens. The two rows (PowerAction::UpdateRestart, UpdateShutDown, added before Count) sit right above Restart and Shut down, follow those options and their confirmation, and call InitiateShutdownW with SHUTDOWN_INSTALL_UPDATES; if that fails, the plain restart or shut down runs instead, except with other accounts signed in (ERROR_SHUTDOWN_USERS_LOGGED_ON): Windows installs updates only with them signed out, so nothing runs and a notice says why.
  • Neon theme (Vice in 3.3, renamed: the name in the settings and texts only, the stored keys islandVice* are the same): choose its colors, five palettes (Sunset, Miami, Synthwave, Toxic and Inferno) or one color of yours, and the island builds the whole neon from it (Look tab, under Colors). A "Pure black background" switch makes its background solid black under the neon, for OLED screens (islandViceBlack, only with Vice on), and "Your own colors under the neon" (islandViceOwnBack) gives the island and its panels your own fill, text and icon colors, solid, with the neon kept; picking one of your own colors with Vice on turns it on instead of switching to the "Your own colors" theme. VicePaletteOf makes a palette from your color in HSV (your hue in the middle, the two ends 40° away, the icons' color across from it and lighter, every color bright enough to glow). The colors are part of the theme (IslandTheme::neon), so they blend like any theme change.
  • Neon theme: animated neon, off by default. The colors flow along the line and it glows like real neon (a brighter core and a wider glow that breathes), with sliders for its speed and strength (50% is the look without them). It runs on its own timer of about 30 steps a second (kViceFlowTimerId, kIdleFrameSeconds between steps at most) only while the option and the theme are on, the island is seen and not over a full-screen app, the animations are on and Windows' energy saver is off. While the island's own frames already run (the visualizer, a transition), it steps inside them instead (StepViceFlow in AnimationFrame) and the timer draws nothing, so there is one stream of draws. A frame where only its step changed is drawn again only where the neon is (m_neonArea, the same partial frames Faísca's picture uses) and only that part goes to the window. On a notch, the glow along the outline is drawn once into a bitmap and reused each frame, dimmed by the breathing (made again only when the shape, colors or strength change). The option says it uses more of the PC.
  • Faísca's small pill when she's alone on the hidden island (ST LOTUS, Discord): "Room on her small pill" (islandPetRoom, %, 100 the room as before, 0 to 300, per profile, slider kSliderPetRoom, dimmed unless she's on the line) scales the room beside her through PetRoomShare: PetLineRect (Island, Fixed, notches), PetSideRect (upright) and the Bar's small pill when only she is on it (HiddenClockRect). With 3.4's Line opacity at 0% the pill is gone and this is her hover room.
  • Brightness wheel step (#7349): a new list under Screen brightness (islandBrightnessStep, per profile, 1/2/5/10%, 5% as before; IslandPref::BrightnessStep, kChoiceBrightnessStep, modeled on the Shelf holds list). BrightnessWheelSteps takes the chosen step from kBrightnessSteps instead of a fixed 5%, so the pill's brightness item and the control center's brightness sliders both follow it; touchpads still keep what's left of a step for the next turn.
  • Weekday in full on the clock (#7562): a new switch, "Weekday in full" (islandWeekdayFull, off, per profile, under "Day of the week" and dimmed while it's off). Island::UpdateClock writes the weekday with dddd instead of ddd in every date order (Windows writes the name in the island's language), so the pill's and the Bar's clocks follow. It keeps today's name and the seven LOCALE_SDAYNAME names, and Island::Layout measures the clock with each of them in place of today's (only when the text or its format changes, m_clockFullKey) and takes the widest, so the pill doesn't change width from one day to the next.
  • Banner size apart from the island (#7759): a new switch, islandBannerApart (IslandPref::BannerApart, off by default, per profile, under Banner size in the Banners section, dimmed without banners). Island::BannerSizeFactor divides the chosen banner size by the island's size when it's on, so the banner keeps the screen's scaling and its own size only; every banner measure, font (UpdateFormats, which now also reformats on the switch) and window room goes through it, in every style and notch.
  • A shortcut for the apps launcher (#7756): a third recorded island shortcut, like the click-through one: islandLauncherKey (IslandPref::LauncherKey, off by default, machine-wide and the main island's) with a SettingKind::Shortcut row (slot 2, islandShortcut2, g_launcherShortcut, no keys until recorded) under Apps (launcher). ShortcutKeyProc takes its keys (bit 128 of g_shortcutKeys) and posts WM_APP_SHORTCUT 6; the island on the main island's monitor with the launcher's notch runs the new Island::OpenLauncherFromShortcut, which toggles m_launcherPanel from its icon (from the island's middle without it, on the Bar too: PanelPlace falls back to the middle when neither the item nor the clock is on it). Over a full-screen app (the island hidden) its keys are pressed again for the app in front, like Win+N and Win+A. SetIslandShortcut and CommandShortcutClashOf refuse keys another island shortcut has; the backup keeps islandShortcut2.
  • Bluetooth headset battery low (#7302): a new status notice, islandNoticeBluetoothLow (IslandPref::NoticeBluetoothLow, NoticeKind::BluetoothLow, off by default, the main island's, under Status notices). While a Bluetooth audio device is connected, the new Island::CheckBluetoothBatteries runs every 5th status round of Tick (no new timer) and reads each one's battery once on a thread (BluetoothBatteryProc, the job's new check); NoteBluetoothBattery tells "Low battery" with its name under 20% and under 10%, each once per discharge by its address (again after it charged 10 points over it), drawn with the connection notice's red ring. The level read as it connects counts too, without a second notice.
  • Banner time (#7302): banners went after a fixed 5 seconds (kBannerShownMs). A new list, islandBannerTime (kChoiceBannerTime, IslandPref::BannerTime, 3/5/8/12/20 s, 5 by default, per profile, in the Banners section, dimmed without banners), and the new BannerShownMs() sets the banner timer in Island::ShowToasts for every banner that goes away by itself; calls, alarms, reminders and a status notice with its own time are as before.
  • A color for each task (#7776): the tasks' editor has a color row (TasksPanel::LayoutColors / DrawColors, Part::ColorPick): none or one of kTaskColors (macOS's eight). Task::color is kept at the end of the stamp field after "#" (TaskColorField / ParseTaskColorField), so old task lists load unchanged and older versions still read the stamp and the day. The task's circle and check take it (TaskTint, blending from the one before through a HoverFades key per change; TaskCheckInk keeps the check readable on yellow), and TaskDay::color carries it to the calendar: the task's circle in a day's list, its mark under the day and its line among the big day's events.
  • What's playing panel: "Song length instead of time left" (islandMediaTotalTime, off by default, per profile, under "Media panel style"): the time at the right of the timeline shows the song's whole length (3:26) instead of the time left (-2:22), in every panel style (MediaRightTime, used by MediaPanel::DrawTimeline); dimmed while the panel can't open, like the style (Discord request).
  • What's playing panel, Pixel style: "Song times always shown" (islandMediaTimesAlways, off by default, per profile, under "Media panel style"): the times under the wavy line stay shown instead of only while it's dragged or under the mouse (MediaTimesShown, used by MediaPanel::DrawTimeline). Switched while the panel is open they fade in or out (m_timesAlways, stepped in MediaPanel::AnimateContents, a frame asked from OnLookChanged, nothing running once it settles). Pixel's times sit 4 dp lower in MediaPlayerLayout, clear of the handle's bottom, so the time under the handle at the song's start or end stays readable (still inside the card's bottom row). Dimmed without the Pixel style ("Only for the Pixel style", its "?" going to the style) and while the panel can't open (Discord request).
  • Four new island languages: the island speaks Indonesian (Bahasa Indonesia), Polish (Polski), Thai (ไทย) and Traditional Chinese (繁體中文), Windhawk's settings page too; choose one in the General tab, or it follows Windows. They join TextLanguage (after Korean, so a saved choice keeps its number; kTextLanguages 11 to 15). Each has its own table (kIndonesianTexts, kPolishTexts, kThaiTexts, kTraditionalChineseTexts: kGermanTexts' keys in its order, so TableText's binary search works), its locale for the dates (kTextLocales), its own name in ChoiceOption, its flag in DrawFlag (Traditional Chinese with Simplified Chinese's flag, their names telling them apart: 简体中文 and 繁體中文), its search words, and Windhawk's settings page ($name, $description and $options for id-ID, pl-PL, th-TH and zh-TW, with the header's @name and @description). The texts are the translators' files (cslavioindo, salackij-bit, notactuallyoak, Parkerlu26) by key, the ones added since their export filled in.
  • The Windows display language goes through the new TextLanguageOfLangId: Traditional Chinese for zh-TW, zh-HK and zh-MO (English before), Indonesian, Polish and Thai by their primary language.
  • Each translator's GitHub name shows beside the language in the languages' lists (kTextTranslators, DrawChoiceName; the lists open wider to the left in DrawDrop, like the icon packs').
  • What's new: older versions have no text in the new languages and read in English (NotesLines takes the first text for a null one); 3.4.0's entry is in the four. The weather's city search sends the language's two letters (zh for both scripts).

Improvements

  • While the island is minimized or hidden as the clock (the Bar too), the Caps Lock, Num Lock and keyboard language bubbles grow out of the line or the clock itself, in its shape, instead of a bubble apart under it (#7520). EdgeTextRect takes the hidden clock's height and place (or the line's), as wide as the text needs, and the shape morphs into it and back; the line's own contents are left out while it shows. Not on an upright pill or with the notches, where the bubble stays as before.
  • Neon theme: "Power menu as a pause menu" (islandVicePause, on by default, per profile): off, the power menu is the usual one in Neon too (VicePauseMenu, which the power panel lays out from).
  • Faísca alone on the hidden island's small pill (no time, timer or what's playing): Line opacity applies to it too (PetPillSeeThrough), so at 0% only she floats at the top; it turns solid again as a banner or a peeking app grows out of it, the edge strip still takes the mouse, in the Island, Fixed and Bar styles and over the Liquid Glass.
  • Neon theme: its texts are easier to read. Bahnschrift is used semi-condensed instead of condensed (UiStretch): the capitals no longer touch at the pill's size, and it stays narrower than the other themes' font.
  • Settings: a choice with several options opens as a list from its field, like Windows' own (DropdownChoice, DrawDrop, drawn in the settings window itself; keyboard and wheel work in it too). Buttons that do something, the picture choices, two-option rows and the setup assistant's choices stay as they were. The window is laid out in two columns: small options are half cards side by side, with their control at the right of the name (a list's field, the style's three choices with a little drawing each, the notches' list with a drawing of each, the color themes as a list with their names and swatches). A dimmed option shows a "?" in the accent beside its name instead of a reason line under it, so cards side by side keep the same height: the mouse on it (or a click) shows the reason in a bubble with a "Change" button, which opens what to change; that bubble springs in once the first is gone. What it changed comes back from an undo arrow beside the option's name, whose own bubble says what goes back (no more link on the card's corner). A list's scroll bar works like the page's: a faint track, wider with the mouse near it, its thumb dragged, a click on the track jumps there. The line under each name is a short one now (a few long names are shortened too), so the cards stay one or two lines tall; resting the mouse on them for a moment shows the whole name and line in a bubble (SettingDescription/SettingName with whole, DrawInfoTip), translated in every language.
  • Tray sizes, clearer (#6162 roadmap): the grid already has its own size (Grid columns, islandTrayColumns); "Other apps' icons before scrolling" (slider 3, g_trayListIcons) only changes the icons opening in the pill, so ControlPanel::SliderDisabled now dims it with the Grid and With names styles, and DisabledReason / DisabledTarget give the existing "Only with the icons opening in the pill" and point at the style's row.
  • Right click on the network button (#7563): with the new option islandActionPages (IslandPref::ActionPages, off by default so nothing changes until it's on, per profile, first in the control center buttons' section), Island::OnMouseButton sends a right click on a control center button of the pill (IslandItem::QuickAction) to its Windows Settings page, from the new PillActionPage(ControlId): Wi-Fi to ms-settings:network, Bluetooth, Night light, Mobile hotspot, Airplane mode, Project and Cast (Display), Captions and Accessibility. The shortcuts have no page and keep showing the settings bubble, as anywhere else on the pill.
  • Lyrics in the title's place (#7330): the hover texts now say where its limit is. "Title width" names the line sung in the title's place too, "Lyrics replace the song title" says the line gets the title's room (raise "Title width" if long lines are cut), and "Longest line on the pill" says that in the title's place "Title width" sets the limit (its own lengths are the lyrics item's). Texts only (the three kDescriptions entries and their 9 translations); no behavior changes.

Fixes

  • What's playing shows play, pause and the next song a moment after you press them on the island, even when the app tells Windows late (#7627). After a play, pause, previous, next or seek sent from the island, the media thread reads the sessions again 0.3, 1 and 3 seconds later (kMediaRereadAfter), as well as on Windows' own change events. Each reading is also given to the island before the cover is read (publish in MediaThreadProc), then again once the cover changed: a reading used to wait for the cover, and a cover that failed lost the whole reading. A missing cover is read again only every kMediaCoverRetrySeconds (3 s) once the song is a few seconds old, not at every event of its app, and a cover that fails no longer loses the whole reading. A song notice for a new title waits for its own cover instead of showing the one carried over from the song before (MediaState::coverCarried, set only when there is a cover, so an app that never sends one still shows the notice at once).
  • A panel opened from the island no longer closes by itself over a game in borderless full screen when the game takes the focus back. On WA_INACTIVE with no mouse button down and the cursor over the panel (FocusTakenWithoutClick), the panel stays and closes once the mouse has been away from it for 0.6 s (kPanelKeptTimerId); a click elsewhere still closes it at once. It stays only while the window in front covers the panel's monitor (CoversMonitor, checked in KeptTick), so Alt+Tab or the Win key to another window closes it.
  • The timer's fill shows on the Bar's line too, while the Bar is hidden as its line, like on the pill's line: the Bar's closing shape draws it with DrawFill(..., asLine) scaled by how far it is into the line, not as the small clock nor with a banner or a text bubble on it.
  • A new alarm's AM/PM button shows the right one when the time format follows Windows (12 hours there) (#7764): that format gives the time whole, with no AM or PM apart, so the button fell back to "AM" while a click did switch the hour to PM (the alarm was saved as PM). It now goes by the hour when no marker comes apart, like the shortcuts' schedule button already did.
  • An app's tray icon no longer shows twice on the island when the app names it in two ways (#7472): OnTrayNotify found an icon by its GUID when the message had one, else by its window and ID, while Windows knows the same icon by both. An app that adds it one way and changes it (or adds it again after the island asks, for apps started before the mod) the other way got a second entry. When the usual look finds nothing, an icon with the same window and ID known the other way is now the same icon, and it takes the GUID when one comes.
  • With "The island handles notifications", Windows' banners no longer come back now and then (#7046): UpdateWindowsQuiet gave Windows' "Do not disturb" up, as if the user had turned it off, in three cases that weren't the user. The island restarting in its process (a monitor change, waking up) turned it off as it closed, and the new one still read it on for a moment (Windows tells the state late, as the code already allowed after turning it on), took it for the user's and gave up a second later: a turn-off by the island less than 5 s ago is now waited out. "Do not disturb" on only by one of Windows' rules (a game, full screen) was left alone as the user's and went off with the rule: DoNotDisturbChosen now tells them apart (asked at most every kDndChosenSeconds, 5 s), and a rule's is taken as the island's own. And after the computer restarted with it on (turnedDndOn kept), off was taken for the user's doing: it's turned on again.
  • The processor's temperature no longer shows a fixed figure some motherboards report (like 17° all the time): only a temperature that changes counts, and with none Windows is taken as not reporting it (#7685). The island reads only Windows' thermal zones, and many boards report a constant in one of them. ThermalZoneWatch keeps each zone's first figure, and a zone counts only once it has changed (CpuTemperatureFrom); none under 20 degrees counts either. With no zone counting after kThermalStuckSeconds (5 minutes), g_cpuTempFound turns 0: the item hides and the settings say Windows doesn't report it. It's looked at again every kThermalLookAgainSeconds (10 minutes) from a fresh watch, as a real zone in whole degrees can stay flat on an idle PC.
  • Dock: icons no longer stay empty for apps whose icon comes a moment after they open (like Fortnite or SteelSeries GG with combined taskbar buttons): the dock looks for it again (#7217). A big icon read as none was kept as none until Explorer restarted, and on a button the taskbar reused for the app the picture was left empty. Now a miss is asked for again 1, 3, 8 and 20 s later, then every 60 s while it's shown (kBigIconRetrySeconds, NoteBigIconRead), with a timer on the taskbar's window drawing the dock then (kBigIconRetryTimerId).
  • The Bar's glass turned solid after hiding and showing again (#7718): GlassLayer::Show set g_glassCompositionFailed on any exception of ShowBlurred (the report's log: E_INVALIDARG as the Bar came back), which kept the glass off until the island restarted. One failure now waits kGlassRetrySeconds and tries again (m_refusedAt, as when Windows refuses its blur), and the glass and shadow geometries never get a negative size or radius.
  • With the Bar hidden as its line or its small pill with the time, a notification banner showed a gap below the line, where the open Bar would be: Island::BannerRect and the banner's drop started at m_pill.bottom. Both now start at the new Island::BarShapeBottom, the bottom of the Bar's shape as it is (following m_hiddenClock, with m_hiddenClockScreen, and m_barLine), so the banner moves with the Bar as it hides or comes back. The small pill (Faísca, the time) keeps what it shows meanwhile: on the Bar the banner is apart from it, so its contents and Faísca's see-through pill no longer go with BannerMorph.

entry.title: Windows Vista/7/8.1 Balloon Notifications Restorer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows Vista/7/8.1 Balloon Notifications Restorer

This mod tries to convert supported Windows 10 and Windows 11 toast notifications into classic notification-area balloons inspired by Windows Vista, 7 and 8.1.

Setup

  • Use a compatible notification area, such as Windows 7/8/8.1 Taskbar Recreation.
  • Restart Explorer after installing the mod. The mod includes an Explorer hook for legacy balloon notifications; an existing Windows legacy balloon policy is also recognized.

Supported notifications are converted on a best-effort basis for selected applications, including Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, PowerShell, Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, Teams, Slack and Outlook. Executable names vary by app version, and inclusion does not guarantee compatibility. Other applications can be added using Windhawk's advanced process inclusion settings.

The mod tries to turn supported toast content into notification-area requests. The notification area determines how those requests are displayed.

Tested on Windows 11 24H2 with Windows 8.1 Taskbar Recreation using a PowerShell notification.

Credits

The Explorer registry-query hook is inspired by Legacy XP-style balloon notifications by Anixx.

entry.title: Windows 8.1 Start Screen Recreation 1.3.0
entry.content:
• Added best-effort live tiles
  • Added support for up to eight custom tiles, each with a target, color, icon, and separate images for the four tile sizes
  • Added best-effort touchscreen support (not tested by the author due to hardware limitations)
  • Reintroduced the optional setting to sample desktop tile colors from application icons (Color sampling is best-effort)
  • Added best-effort integration with Windows 8.1 Taskbar Recreation: when detected on the current monitor, it is prioritized on bottom-edge hover. The native taskbar remains the fallback when the companion is not detected
  • Preserved the existing layout format. Custom images are read from local paths and are not copied by the mod
  • Standardized and translated the new settings’ descriptions
  • Applied minor graphic improvements

entry.title: Disable taskbar per monitor 1.0
entry.content:
Disable taskbar per monitor

Pick one or more monitors. Their taskbar is disabled: it's invisible, can't be clicked, and never comes back, whether from the mouse at the screen edge, the Win key, Win+T / Win+number, flashing app buttons or notifications. Windows on those monitors can use the space the taskbar took. Taskbars on every other monitor are left alone. Works with the taskbar at the bottom, top, left or right, with auto-hide on or off.

Why not auto-hide

Auto-hide brings the taskbar back on hover, on the Win key and when an app wants attention, and it applies to every monitor. Taskbar auto-hide fine tuning can keep it from ever showing, but on all monitors at once, and Taskbar auto-hide per monitor chooses auto-hide on or off per monitor but doesn't stop the taskbar from showing. This mod turns the taskbar off on the chosen monitors only and doesn't need or change the auto-hide setting.

Choosing monitors

The Monitors to disable the taskbar on setting is a comma-separated list. Each entry can be:

  • primary: the primary monitor, wherever it is.
  • A number (1, 2, 3...): the monitor's position in Windows' monitor enumeration. It may differ from the numbers shown in Display Settings, and it can change after plugging monitors in or out.
  • Any other text: matched (case-insensitive) against part of the monitor's device name, model name or interface name, e.g. GSM5BD2 or DISPLAY2. This stays correct when the numbering changes.

Examples: primary · 1,3 · primary, GSM5BD2. An empty list disables nothing.

To see the number, device name, model and interface name of each monitor: Advanced tab, set Debug logging to Mod logs, open Show log output, then save the settings again. Every monitor is logged in a Monitor line.

How it works

The taskbar window of a chosen monitor and its popups (tooltips, previews) are cloaked with DWM, which makes them invisible and click-through without moving them, and the work area of that monitor is computed as if its taskbar were auto-hidden. Nothing is written to the system settings, so disabling or removing the mod leaves no trace.

Notes

  • Windows 11. Tested on build 26300 with bottom and left taskbars, auto-hide on and off. "Show my taskbar on all displays" must be on if any of the chosen monitors is not the primary one.
  • Keyboard focus can still move to a disabled taskbar (e.g. Win+T); press Esc to leave it.

entry.title: Volume Key Step 1.0
entry.content:
Volume Key Step

Windows raises or lowers the volume by 2% per volume key press. This mod lets you pick any step from 1% to 100%. The Windows volume flyout still shows as usual.

The step also applies to anything else that steps the volume through Explorer, such as scrolling with the Windows 11 indicator in the Taskbar Volume Control mod.

At least one audio device (speaker or mic) must be connected when Explorer starts. If none was, reload the mod after connecting one.

entry.title: Notepad Pro 1.0.0
entry.content:
Notepad Pro

Upgrade the standard Windows Notepad with modern code-editor features while keeping it fast and lightweight.

Line-Number Gutter

Adds a clean line-number margin to the left side of the editor.

  • Smart wrapping: Only displays numbers on the first row of wrapped lines.
  • Dynamic sizing: Automatically adjusts its width as your document grows.
  • Theme-aware: Seamlessly adapts to light and dark modes in real time.
  • Editor sync: Matches your current font, size, zoom level, and display scaling, with highlighting for the active line.
  • Markers: Colors the left edge of the gutter next to every line you changed, added, or removed.

Minimap

Adds a high-level visual overview of your entire file right alongside the scrollbar.

  • Visual preview: Represents your text as clean, color-coded blocks for easy scanning.
  • Smooth navigation: Click anywhere to jump directly to that section, drag the viewport slider, or scroll smoothly with your mouse wheel.
  • Responsive layout: Automatically scales with the window size and hides itself when the window becomes too narrow.
  • Universal support: Works across all open documents and file types.

Syntax Highlighting

Automatically brings color and readability to popular programming and data files based on the open file type.

  • Rich color coding: Highlights keywords, types, strings, numbers, and directives while keeping plain text and unsaved tabs clean.
  • Non-destructive: Purely visual, never alters your underlying files.
  • Theme-aware: Uses tailored color palettes that automatically switch between light and dark themes.

Note: Very large files may cause slight delays, slower rendering, or higher memory usage when calculating line numbers, drawing the minimap, or running syntax highlighting.

More Features Soon

This mod is under active development, with additional quality-of-life improvements and editor tools planned for future updates.

entry.title: Taskbar Battery Icon Customizer 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Battery Icon Customizer

Give the Windows 11 taskbar battery icon a new look - no coding needed.

  • Apple iOS style - a solid pill with the percentage cut out of it, green while charging, yellow in battery saver and red when low.
  • Classic style - the older, compact single-color Windows 11 battery.
  • Percentage only - replace the icon with just the number, with your choice of size, weight, font, % sign, charging bolt and an optional colored or outlined pill behind it.
  • Your own colors - pick a color for every state (on battery, charging, plugged in, battery saver, low, very low) from simple lists.
  • Battery percentage - next to the icon or inside the battery.
  • Animations - bounce, zoom or flash when you plug in; shake, drop or flash when you unplug; a "filling up" or breathing effect while charging; and a pulse or blink when the battery is low.
  • Size and spacing - make it bigger or line it up with the Wi-Fi and volume icons.

Getting started

  1. Open the Settings tab.
  2. Choose a look from Quick look (for example Apple iOS) and click Save settings. The taskbar updates right away.

Want something else? Set Quick look to Build my own, then choose:

  • Icon style - Windows 11, Classic Windows 11, Apple iOS, or Percentage only (then fine-tune it under Percentage-only style).
  • Color mode - Automatic, Single color, or My own colors (then pick a color for each battery state from the lists under Colors).
  • Show battery percentage - off, next to the icon, or inside it.
  • Size and spacing and Animations - these apply to every look, including Quick looks. Turn on "Preview the charger animations" to see the plug-in and unplug animations each time you save.

Need an exact shade? Pick Custom in a color list and type a hex code such as #FF4545 in the matching field of Exact colors at the bottom.

Tips

  • Single color but red when the battery is low: Color mode My own colors, set every color to Same as the taskbar text, and Low battery to Red.
  • Automatic colors in the Apple style follow iOS: white (or black on a light taskbar) normally, green when charging, yellow in battery saver and red at or below the low battery level.
  • If Windows' own "Battery percentage" option is on, the mod hides it while it shows its own percentage, so it never appears twice.

Requires a Windows 11 build with the new colored battery icon (Windows 11 24H2/25H2 builds from late 2025 onwards).

entry.title: Twinkle Brightness 1.1.0
entry.content:
Twinkle Brightness

Control the brightness of all your displays - external monitors and laptop screens - from a tray icon or the keyboard. Inspired by the excellent Twinkle Tray app, re-imagined as a lightweight Windhawk mod with no Electron runtime.

Features

  • Tray panel: click the sun icon in the notification area to get a brightness slider for every display. The panel follows the Windows light/dark theme and accent color.
  • Link displays: the chain button in the panel links the displays. While linked, one slider controls all displays and the hotkeys change all of them. Linked displays are always set to the same level: the first change brings them together. To make displays that differ in brightness look alike at the same level, use the per-display minimum and maximum. While unlinked, each display has its own slider and the hotkeys change the display with the active window.
  • Hotkeys: bind any key combination to increase, decrease or set the brightness, turn the displays off, or open the panel. A hotkey can also target a specific display.
  • On-screen indicator: a small overlay shows the new level when you use a hotkey, with one row per display when they are at different levels.
  • Schedule: change the brightness automatically at given times of the day, with a smooth transition.
  • Idle dimming: dim the displays after a period of inactivity and restore them as soon as you touch the mouse or keyboard.
  • Per-display options: custom names, hiding displays, and min/max brightness to normalize displays that are brighter or darker than others.
  • Tray menu: refresh displays, turn displays off, pause automatic brightness, and copy display names/IDs for use in the settings.

How it works

  • External monitors are controlled with DDC/CI (VCP code 0x10), the same channel the monitor's own on-screen menu uses. DDC/CI must be enabled in the monitor's menu. Some docks, adapters, KVM switches and VGA/DVI connections do not pass DDC/CI through.
  • Laptop and tablet screens are controlled through WMI, like the Windows brightness slider.

The mod runs in its own dedicated windhawk.exe process (Windhawk "tool mod") and does not inject code into Explorer or any other program.

Hotkey format

Combine Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Win with one key, separated by +, for example Ctrl+Alt+Up, Win+Shift+PageDown or Ctrl+Alt+F1. Supported keys: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F24, Up, Down, Left, Right, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End, Insert, Delete, Space, Plus, Minus, NumpadPlus, NumpadMinus, Numpad0-Numpad9.

Choosing displays in the settings

Hotkeys, schedule entries and per-display options accept a part of a display's name (as shown in the panel) or ID. Right-click the tray icon and choose Copy display info to copy the names and IDs of all connected displays. Leave the field empty to target all displays (for hotkeys: to follow the link button).

Troubleshooting

  • A monitor says "not supported": enable DDC/CI in its on-screen menu, use a direct HDMI/DisplayPort/USB-C cable instead of a dock or adapter, then choose Refresh displays in the tray menu.
  • A monitor stops responding after sleep: choose Refresh displays, or turn the monitor off and on with its power button.
  • A hotkey does nothing: another program may already use that combination. Check the Windhawk log for "RegisterHotKey failed". The default Ctrl+Alt+Up/Ctrl+Alt+Down are also used by Visual Studio Code (add a cursor) and some Intel graphics drivers (rotate the screen); change them in the settings if you need those shortcuts.
  • The AMD Radeon software can interfere with DDC/CI brightness. Disable "Custom Colors" there if brightness changes have no effect.

This mod is not affiliated with Twinkle Tray or its author.

entry.title: AutoClean 2.2026.2211
entry.content:
AutoClean

Silent, event-driven background Temp folder and Recycle Bin cleaner running in a dedicated Windhawk Tool Mod process.

Action Triggers — Temp & Recycle Bin

Icon Shortcut / Trigger Action
🖱️ 3x Left-Click (Desktop & Taskbar empty space) Clean Temp folders immediately and show OLED corner toast
🖱️ Middle-Click (1x/2x/3x, Desktop & Taskbar empty space) Empty Recycle Bin immediately and show OLED corner toast
🚀 Windows Login / Startup Clean Temp folders (and optionally Recycle Bin) automatically after login
📦 Size Limit (KB/MB/GB/TB) Prune oldest items first or full sweep when Temp or Recycle Bin hits limit
🔢 File Count Limit (X items) Prune oldest-deleted items or empty Recycle Bin at X items
⏱️ Timer / Retention Clean Temp on a repeating schedule and expire Recycle Bin items older than your retention window
⚠️ Low Disk Space Emergency Free Temp and oldest Recycle Bin items on the low-space drive when free space crosses below the floor

How AutoClean Differs from Windows Storage Sense

Windows Storage Sense covers basic periodic Temp and Recycle Bin cleanup, whereas AutoClean adds:

  • True Event-Driven Watching: Uses ReadDirectoryChangesW for %TEMP% and SHChangeNotifyRegister on the Recycle Bin so idle CPU and disk usage stay at zero (secondary HDDs can spin down normally).
  • AI Agent %TEMP% Protection: Preserves local %TEMP% scratchpads and worktrees created by AI coding & desktop agents (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Windsurf, Goose, Aider, Copilot, MCP) by default.
  • Instant Empty-Space Mouse Shortcuts: Triple left-click empty Desktop/Taskbar space to clean Temp, or middle-click empty space to empty the Recycle Bin, with UI Automation checks so taskbar buttons and desktop icons are never triggered.
  • Granular Controls & Smart Deferral: Exact KB/MB/GB/TB size caps, oldest-first pruning to a target percentage, wildcard exclusions, fullscreen/battery deferral, single-shot Dry-Run simulation, and borderless OLED corner toasts.

Safety Guards

  • Temp Path Validation: Refuses to clean drive roots, %windir%, %USERPROFILE%, or known user folders (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, Videos, AppData) if %TEMP% is misconfigured.
  • Minimum Age Grace Periods: Honored on all Temp sweeps (default 24 hours / 1440 minutes) and Recycle Bin pruning (default 24 hours / 1440 minutes) so active installers, build tools, PyInstaller payloads, and recent deletions stay protected.
  • Reparse-Point & Attribute Safety: Skips junctions/symlinks, respects Windows file locks, and restores Read-Only/Hidden/System attributes if a locked file cannot be deleted.
  • Safe Recycle Bin Defaults: Automatic Recycle Bin size/count thresholds and startup cleaning are off by default; only 30-day age expiry is enabled out of the box.

entry.title: ZoomIt 1.3.0
entry.content:
ZoomIt

Zoom into any part of your screen and draw on it, straight from a hotkey. It works like Sysinternals ZoomIt, without a separate app running in the tray.

Features

  • Zoom with Ctrl+1. The screen under your mouse zooms in smoothly. Scroll or use the arrow keys to zoom further, and move the mouse to look around.
  • Draw with Ctrl+2. Draw on the screen as it is, or click while zoomed to draw on the zoomed view.
  • Shapes and highlighters. Hold Shift for a straight line, Ctrl for a box, Tab for a circle and Ctrl+Shift for an arrow. Shift plus a color key gives a see-through highlighter.
  • Text and blur. Press T to type on the screen and X to blur out private details.
  • Copy or save. Ctrl+C copies what you see and Ctrl+S saves it as a picture. Add Shift to pick an area first.
  • Works over admin windows. The hotkeys and drawing keep working while an app that runs as administrator is in front.
  • Your settings. Hotkeys, zoom level and speed, animation, pen color (six colors, system, the Windows accent color or your own hex), pen size, highlighter and blur strength, text font and size, save folder.

Keys while zoomed or drawing

Key What it does
Mouse wheel, Up, Down Zoom in or out
Left click Start drawing while zoomed
Right click Stop drawing, or leave
Esc Leave
R, G, B, Y, O, P Red, green, blue, yellow, orange or pink pen
Shift + a color key Highlighter in that color
X Blur pen
Ctrl + wheel, Ctrl + Up or Down Pen size, or text size while typing
Hold Shift, Ctrl, Tab or Ctrl+Shift while dragging Line, box, circle or arrow
T, Shift+T Type text, lined up left or right
W, K White or black board
E Erase all drawings
Ctrl+Z Undo the last drawing
Space Move the mouse to the middle of the screen
Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Shift+C Copy the screen, or an area of it
Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Shift+S Save the screen, or an area of it

Notes

  • Turn off ZoomIt in PowerToys or the ZoomIt app first. Two apps can't use the same hotkey.
  • Write hotkeys like Ctrl+1, Ctrl+Shift+Z or Win+Alt+F2. Leave one empty to turn it off.

How it differs from WinDraw and Taskbar Snipper

WinDraw and Taskbar Snipper mark up the screen at its normal size. ZoomIt is a tool for presenting: it zooms into a still picture of the screen first, and you draw on the zoomed view, with a blur pen and text, on Sysinternals ZoomIt's own keys. If you only want to mark up the screen, WinDraw has more drawing tools.

Credits

Works like ZoomIt by Mark Russinovich (Sysinternals). Written from scratch for Windhawk; it shares no code with ZoomIt. MIT.

To read text bigger under the mouse, try Hover Text Magnifier by Math Shamenson.

entry.title: Shell Font Changer Plus 1.4.2
entry.content:
Shell Font Changer Plus

Change the text font in File Explorer to any font you have installed, and make the text bigger or smaller. Icons and emoji keep their own glyphs, so buttons never turn into empty boxes.

Features

  • File Explorer text. The file list, the navigation pane and the column headers follow the font you pick.
  • Icons and emoji stay intact. Symbol and icon fonts keep their own glyphs, so buttons never show empty boxes.
  • Text size. Scale File Explorer's text from 75% to 200%. Rows, columns and boxes are laid out for the new size, headings stay larger than body text, and each monitor keeps its own scaling. The size covers all text Explorer draws itself: the desktop labels, context menus, the Run, Properties and copy dialogs, and the Windows 10 taskbar.
  • Weight is kept. Semibold and bold text stays semibold and bold.
  • Classic, themed and modern text. GDI text, visual-style themes and DirectWrite layouts are all covered.
  • Text fits its controls. Text that would overflow shrinks a little, to no less than 85% of its height or 80% of its width. If classic text still overflows, the original UI font draws it.
  • Clean to remove. The mod writes nothing to the registry, so turning it off leaves nothing behind.

How to use

Type an installed font family name in the settings, such as FiraCode Nerd Font or Inter. The field starts empty, so nothing changes until you pick a font. Leave it empty, or type None, to keep the original font.

Set Text size to make the text bigger or smaller. It is a percentage of the size Windows picks: 100 keeps it as it is, 125 makes it a quarter bigger. It works with or without a font. With the font empty and the size at 100, the mod does nothing.

If the font is not installed, or its name is 32 characters or longer, the font is left as it is and the Windhawk log says why. The text size still applies.

Settings apply without reloading the mod. Explorer sizes its rows and boxes when it creates a window's fonts, so a new text size shows in windows opened after the change. Restart Explorer to resize the desktop and the windows that were already open, and again after turning the size back to 100 or turning the mod off. Turning the mod off and on again, or updating it, without that restart can make some text grow twice, and a restart fixes it.

To fit its box, text drawn by DirectWrite never shrinks below its original size when only the size is changed, or below 85% of it with a font set. Text that ends in "..." keeps its size and its "...".

The Windows 11 command bar and address bar, Start, Search and Settings are drawn by XAML or web views and keep their fonts. The Windows 11 File Explorer Styler, Start Menu Styler and Settings Styler can set fonts there. Windows that were already open may need to be reopened.

Turn off the original Explorer Font Changer before you turn this one on. Change More Fonts also changes fonts as they are created. If you use it, leave this mod's font empty so only one of them picks the font.

Credits

Based on Explorer Font Changer by Gabriela Cristei. MIT. The text size scales each font in proportion when it is created, the approach worked out in wodenwhel's Explorer Font Size Changer.

entry.title: No-Click Touchpad: Tap & Hold 1.1
entry.content:
• Added a "Taps to right-click" setting. With two taps, a single tap in the corner does nothing and a quick double tap right-clicks.
  • "Two taps, one tap left-clicks" works the same, but a single corner tap left-clicks about half a second later.

entry.title: Touchpad Relaxed Hand Tracking 1.2.1
entry.content:
• Steadier speed multiplier (improved "flicks"): the higher multiplier no longer drops at the start and end of each movement, when fingers don't move in unison (most noticeable with five fingers down). The lower multiplier now only takes over after a confirmed movement with fewer fingers.
  • No more accidental clicks with five fingers resting: touchpads usually report up to five contacts, and a thumb split in two at the pad's edge made the pad take turns among them; those swaps no longer click.
  • 5-3 fingers moving default speed Increased to 2.0 after this update's precision gain.
  • Readme and settings review.

entry.title: Nimbus Menu 2.0.0
entry.content:
• Tray: the icons of the apps running in the background, next to the status area. Inline with arrows, behind one button (pin the ones you want outside), or in a grid or list panel. Clicks go to the app itself; the middle button pins; drag an icon onto another to reorder.
  • Control center: one dock button opens do not disturb, Bluetooth, night light, shortcuts (project, cast, captions, accessibility), each monitor's brightness (DDC/CI), sound, power and any other item placed there. Each item opens its full panel inside it, and it scrolls on small screens.
  • Every status item can be in the dock, the control center and Start at once, or off.
  • Bluetooth: turn it on and off, paired devices with their battery, connect and disconnect headsets and speakers.
  • Notifications: Windows' notifications also show as Nimbus cards (corner of your choice, paused under the mouse, never over games), with their buttons; a bell opens the list, newest first; Win+N can open it. Optional: hide Windows' own banners (asks first, restored when turned off). Its own sounds (15 to pick, or Windows' own), one for notifications and one for reminders.
  • Player: what any app plays in Windows' media controls: cover, title, time, controls, shuffle and repeat, that app's volume, switch between apps. In the dock as the cover and title, the cover, the title, bars moving with the sound, or an icon.
  • Devices: wireless batteries (Bluetooth, Xbox controllers, and USB receivers through BatteryHub when installed), with warnings at 20% and 10%.
  • Notes and reminders: notes stay until deleted; reminders come as Nimbus notifications, late too if the PC was off.
  • Shelf: drop files on the dock to keep them for a moment, then drag them anywhere; Ctrl+V turns a copied picture or text into a file.
  • Start: smarter search (no accents needed, initials like "vsc", one typo, common nicknames, what you open most first), keyboard navigation in every tab, power buttons that ask before restart or shut down, and a right-click menu with sign out, hibernate and restart to advanced options. All apps refreshes when an app is installed or removed.
  • Power modes follow Windows' power plans (High performance, Balanced, Power saver).
  • Its own settings window with a live preview; Windhawk's settings tab is empty on purpose (1.x settings carry over). A guided setup asks a few questions on the first run.
  • Follows Windows' high contrast and "Animation effects" off.
  • Start's Status tab in the control center's look (time, player, round switches, sliders, tray, power, rows), its parts in any order ("Organize": drag them, or Alt + arrows), saved per account.
  • Sound panel, simple (the default, as before) or complete (Settings › Status area › Sound): the apps playing on the left and every output on the right. Drag an app onto an output to play it there too, from one output to another to move it, × to take it off one; choose the default output and the one for calls. Complete is off by default because it changes Windows' sound output: the default and communications outputs (IPolicyConfig) and each app's output (the AudioPolicyConfig factory Windows' own Sound settings use), both undocumented by Microsoft; an app on a second output is a copy Nimbus plays through process loopback (documented, Windows 10 2004+) while it runs. An app that picks its own outputs (TeamSpeak, Discord) is muted on the one it's taken off. Going back to Simple puts everything back (every app on the default, copies off, those mutes undone). Listed in the readme's "What it changes in Windows".
  • Notification sounds stay audible during calls (Nimbus' audio session opts out of Windows' communications ducking).
  • Many fixes: dock clicks on admin windows, panels anchored to their item, faster panels (slow reads moved to worker threads).
